cards.example: However, the partner bank has not yet confirmed the format.

cards.back: but (neutral) / though, at end of sentence (informal)
cards.example: The fix works. It's a bit slow, though.
Although the tests passed, we found a bug in staging.

cards.back: despite / in spite of + noun or -ing
cards.example: Despite the outage, all orders were processed by noon.
The backend is stable, whereas the frontend still needs work.
On the other hand, a managed service reduces our maintenance effort.
The certificate expired; therefore, the connection was refused.
As a result, several clients could not sign their contracts.
The release was delayed due to a regression in onboarding.
Since the vendor is down, we'll retry the orders tonight.
In addition, the new flow reduces manual checks by half.
What's more, the new cluster costs less to run.
As well as fixing the bug, we improved the logging.

cards.back: for example / for instance / such as + noun
cards.example: Some services, such as onboarding, need extra monitoring.
Response times improved, in particular on the order endpoint.

cards.back: in other words / that is (formal, written)
cards.example: In other words, we need two more weeks of testing.
First of all, let's look at what happened last night.
Next, the file is validated and loaded into the database.
Lastly, we need to agree on the go-live date.
Eventually, we rolled back and fixed it the next day.

cards.back: to conclude (formal) / to sum up / all in all
cards.example: To sum up, the migration was a success.

cards.front: in realtà / a dire il vero
cards.example: Actually, the issue was on the partner bank's side.

cards.back: as far as ... is concerned / regarding / as for
cards.example: As far as security is concerned, we follow the bank's policy.
In terms of cost, the managed option is clearly cheaper.
With regard to your request, we will reply by Friday.
By the way, the staging database will be down tomorrow.
Anyway, let's get back to the release checklist.
We need the keys today; otherwise, testing will slip.
We'll go live on Monday unless the regression tests fail.
We can deploy tonight, provided that the PM signs off.

cards.back: if / in the event that (formal) (NOT 'in case' = per precauzione)
cards.example: In the event that the job fails, the on-call engineer is paged.

cards.back: so that / in order to + verb
cards.example: We added retries so that transient errors don't block orders.
In the meantime, please use the manual reconciliation process.
Once the fix is merged, I'll trigger the pipeline.
Keep the feature flag off until the vendor confirms.
Essentially, the service acts as a gateway to the fund platform.
That said, the current solution is good enough for now.
In contrast, the old system needed a full day to reconcile.
Similarly, the emails module will move to the new queue.
To be honest, I don't think the deadline is realistic.
